summary: reactjs-risk preinstall exfiltrates host identifiers via DNS to attacker-controlled logger
details: On npm install, scripts.preinstall runs `node poc.js`, which executes `whoami` and reads `os.hostname()` and `os.platform()`, hex-encodes the concatenated result, and issues a DNS resolution for `<hex>.z4wwii.dnslog.cn`, exfiltrating the installer's username, hostname, and platform out-of-band to a public DNS logging service. The module identifiers for `dns`, `os`, and `child_process`, and the `whoami` command string, are assembled via string concatenation (`'d'+'n'+'s'`, `'wh'+'oa'+'mi'`) to evade static detection. The package name resembles a React-related library but ships no legitimate React functionality; its sole install-time effect is the DNS beacon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
